Daily KRW trend analysis.text:
**☀️ KRW morning brief: Tue 10 Nov 2026, 08:10 SGT**

**1. Rates**
- **USD/KRW:** **1,347.1** at the Seoul close (3:30pm KST, Mon 9 Nov). That's 9.5 won stronger for the won than Friday's 1,356.6. It opened at 1,363.0. A week earlier (Mon 2 Nov close) it was 1,343.8, so the won is about 0.25% weaker over the week. It hit 1,361.8 on 6 Nov, a one-month high, and its 2026 low was 1,323.1 on 26 Oct.
- **SGD/KRW:** about **1,053**. I worked this out from the Seoul close and USD/SGD at 1.2788 (Trading Economics, 9 Nov). XE showed **1,061.7** (8 Nov, 17:03 UTC), so SGD buys roughly 0.8% fewer won than over the weekend. I couldn't find a reliable 1-week SGD/KRW figure.
- ⚠️ **Sources disagree:** Investing.com shows SGD/KRW at 1,105.8 with no date. That doesn't fit the USD/KRW and USD/SGD figures, so treat it as unreliable. Its USD/KRW quote (1,324.9) also looks stale.
- **🎯 Distance to 1,150 target:** about **97 KRW away (~9.2%)**. Measured from XE's 1,061.7, it's about 88 KRW (~8.3%).

**2. Why the won moved**
- **AI/chip sell-off and foreign selling:** The KOSPI fell 11.7% in the week of 2–6 Nov on worries about AI spending. Foreigners sold a net ~10.4T won of Korean stocks that week, mostly Samsung and SK Hynix. Monday was their 7th straight day of net selling (~0.6–0.7T won). The KOSPI clung to 5,019 (−0.81%).
- **Exporters selling dollars:** This was the main support on Monday. Dealers say exporters waited for 1,360s to convert their dollars, which effectively caps the won's weakness. Korea's record September current-account surplus adds to that support.
- **Strong US dollar:** October payrolls came in at +165k vs ~65k expected. Markets now put ~77% odds on a Fed **hike** in December. DXY is at ~102.3 and the US 10-year yield at ~4.86–4.87% (as of Fri 6 Nov).
- **Oil drop helps a bit:** Brent fell to ~$92 (down ~6% on Fri 6 Nov), which is good for Korea as an oil importer. SGD has firmed slightly (USD/SGD −0.31% on 9 Nov).

**3. What to watch**
- **Tonight, 9:30pm SGT:** US October CPI (headline forecast ~3.7% y/y). A hot number means more Fed-hike bets and a stronger dollar.
- **Wed 11 Nov, ~6am SGT:** CoreWeave Q3 results, a key test of the mood around AI and chip stocks.
- **Thu 12 Nov:** KOSPI 200 options expiry. **Fri 13 Nov, 9:30pm SGT:** US PPI.
- **26 Nov:** Bank of Korea decision (rate is 3.00%, held in October after hikes). **8–9 Dec:** Fed meeting.

**4. Bottom line**
Forces are pulling both ways. The strong dollar, Fed-hike bets and foreign selling of Korean stocks push the won weaker. Exporters selling dollars around 1,360 and Korea's big surplus push back. BofA expects USD/KRW at 1,330 by year-end, which would mean a firmer won, not a weaker one. On its own, 1,150 per SGD would need the won to weaken ~9% against SGD. That looks unlikely in the next few days, but tonight's CPI and AI-stock sentiment are big swing factors. Uncertainty is high.

_Not financial advice._

Daily AI newsletter.text:
## Your daily AI brief: Monday, 9 Nov 2026

**Today in AI:** Anthropic ships new frontier models days before its IPO, and Nvidia's stock slides as its board investigates Jensen Huang.

---

### Top stories

**Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2**
Anthropic released two versions of the same new model. Fable 5.2 is available to everyone and keeps its cyber and bio safeguards, though it blocks about 55% fewer requests than 5.1. Mythos 5.2 drops those limits and is only for verified life-sciences and security organizations. Anthropic says output is up to 30% faster, and API pricing is $8 in / $40 out per million tokens, which Fortune says is about 20% below OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.
*Why it matters:* This is likely Anthropic's last big launch before its IPO, and it's competing on price as well as performance.

**Nvidia shares drop ~4% as its board probes Jensen Huang**
Nvidia's board opened an inquiry into whether Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence, following reports of his relationship with a former executive at a partner company. The board says it has no reason to believe any secrets were compromised. Huang told staff he'll cooperate fully.
*Why it matters:* Huang is the face of the AI chip boom, so any doubt about his leadership hits a $4.5T company that the whole sector relies on.

**Anthropic spends $3.4B on gas generators for its data centers**
The FT reports that Anthropic agreed to pay about $3.4B for 1.7 GW of gas-powered generators. It took over existing orders from Texas-based OnePWR Solutions. The deal reportedly closed in September and became public this weekend.
*Why it matters:* AI labs are now buying their own power plants because they can't wait for the grid.

**Nominal triples its valuation to $3B**
The Austin startup, which makes AI software for testing hardware like aircraft and nuclear reactors, raised a $240M Series C led by Lightspeed and Insight. That's up from a $1B valuation in March. It also won a $71.2M Air Force award in October.
*Why it matters:* AI for defense and physical engineering is one of the hottest areas in venture funding right now.

---

### Quick hits

- 🐋 DeepSeek's agent platform, Harness, says it now has 1.54M daily users, up by more than 1M in a month.
- 🎤 Suno was hit with two more copyright lawsuits, from the owners of Elvis Presley's music rights and Eminem's publisher.
- 🧪 In an Alibaba real-world test, the best coding agent fully finished only 26.4% of tasks, even though it scores near-perfect on older benchmarks.
- 🍎 Apple's new CEO is reportedly pushing for faster AI development, and Siri could become more agent-like as early as 2027.

---

### Tool of the day

**OpenCode Browse:** an MCP server plus Chromium extension that lets coding agents (OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) work in your real browser, with your tabs and logins. It hands logins, 2FA and payments back to you, can limit agents to approved sites, and records screenshots and network traffic. It's available now and open source.
